source.author: lucan
source.text: His praeter Latias acies erat impiger Astur, Vettonesque leves, profugique a gente vetusta Gallorum Celtae, miscentes nomen Iberis.
source.text_original: His praeter Latias acies erat impiger Astur, / Vettonesque leves, profugique a gente vetusta / Gallorum Celtae, miscentes nomen Iberis.
source.text_english: Besides these stood the energetic Asturian troops, the lightly armed Vettones, and the Celts who had fled from the ancient race of the Gauls, mingling their name with the Iberians.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: De quibus pulchre Lucanus: Gallorum Celtae miscentes nomen Iberis: quos nos possumus Gallohispanos dicere.
reuse.text_original: De quibus pulchre Lucanus: Gallorum Celtae miscentes nomen Iberis: quos nos possumus Gallohispanos dicere.
reuse.text_english: On these Lucan says well: the Celts of Gaul, mixing their name with the Iberians: whom we can call Gaul-Hispanics.
